cases.before: V0.2 original: 6 nodes (IMPLEMENT/REVIEW/REPAIR/REVIEW/MERGE/FINAL_GATE), role-on-MERGE defect, quality 1. V0.3: empty decline (HUMAN_GATE reachability), unscored.
cases.notes: Same correct empty decline as V0.3, now with a more specific, actionable warning: 'Start a separate later planning run from an executable node after acceptance, then add IMPLEMENT, REVIEW, and REPAIR there.' Not a complexity case at all once the anchor is recognized as a HUMAN_GATE -- V0.2's original over-complexity (MERGE-as-generic-aggregator, extra FINAL_GATE) was a symptom of the model attempting an unreachable structure, not a pure complexity failure; the complexity rules cannot be exercised at this anchor and this case is retained per the evaluation's 'do not replace difficult cases' instruction, not because it independently tests V0.4's changes.

cases.before: V0.2: 2 nodes/5 edges, quality 3. V0.3: 2 nodes/8 edges (2 redundant FALLBACK-to-HUMAN_REQUIRED edges beyond V0.2's shape), quality 2, unnecessary_complexity=true.
cases.notes: Improved back toward V0.2's leaner shape: edge count fell from 8 (V0.3) to 6, and FIRST_MATCH is now used with a single unconditional catch-all (declared last) instead of enumerating both has_findings values explicitly plus a separate 'unclassified' fallback -- the exact FIRST_MATCH-catch-all pattern the package's own unconditional_edge_id addition (V0.3) highlights. complexity_score 2, not 3: the second REVIEW node (escalation for has_findings=True) is defensible but not provably required -- a single-node design (V0.2's very first baseline) is also legal. quality_score 3: legal, correctly ordered, reasonably scoped, an operator would plausibly accept as-is.

cases.before: V0.2/V0.3: identical 3-node REVIEW->REPAIR->REVIEW loop, quality 2, unnecessary_complexity flagged.
cases.notes: The single largest before/after swing in this stage: 3 nodes/8 edges -> 1 node/2 edges. The model reinterpreted 'make this more robust' as a single hardening IMPLEMENT step feeding directly into the EXISTING review, rather than fabricating an entire REVIEW->REPAIR->REVIEW loop. No structural element can be removed without losing the requested semantics (a hardening step, reviewed by the existing review) -- complexity_score 3. Direct, clean evidence the required-vs-optional and review-discipline rules changed behavior, not just wording.

cases.before: No V0.2/V0.3 equivalent -- new case, built specifically to test whether REPAIR's continuation reuses an existing node instead of fabricating a new REVIEW.
cases.notes: THE direct test of V0.4's single most evidence-grounded rule. Result: exactly 2 nodes (REVIEW + REPAIR), and REPAIR's successful (outcome=PASS) continuation routes to the EXISTING N02 review -- the model's own assumption states this explicitly: 'The existing review can legally receive either a direct PASS transition from the added review or a successful transition from the repair.' No third review node was fabricated. complexity_score 2, not 3: REPAIR's non-PASS outcomes (BLOCKED, FAIL, INVALID) were each given a separate FALLBACK edge to HUMAN_REQUIRED (3 edges) rather than one unconditional catch-all declared last, the same collapsing trick E_first_match_hazard's own N10 uses for a comparable case -- a real, minor, edge-level residual pattern, not a node-level one. quality_score 3: legal, correct, and the core structural question (does it reuse the existing review) was answered correctly.

cases.before: No V0.2/V0.3 equivalent -- new case, phrased ('both the codebase and the design docs') to tempt a spurious fan-out+MERGE for what one node can do.
cases.notes: Built exactly one node whose own instructions cover both sources, with no branch and no MERGE. Direct, clean positive evidence for the branch/MERGE-discipline rules: 'gather from two sources' was correctly read as one responsibility, not two independent perspectives requiring isolation and rejoin.

aggregate_metrics.schema_envelope_valid_rate: 8/8 (100%) -- the one non-READY case was a well-reasoned, closed-set PROPOSAL_SHAPE decline, not a malformed output
aggregate_metrics.caveat: This is a small (8-call), single-pass, deliberately-curated corpus: 3 of V0.2/V0.3's hardest structurally-blocked cases (G_human_gate, RP1_impl_review_repair, J_merge_and_human_gate) were intentionally NOT rerun here because they are already well-understood, non-complexity failures (HUMAN_GATE reachability / zero node budget) whose outcome does not depend on anything V0.4 changed -- rerunning them would have re-confirmed known behavior without adding complexity evidence, at real live-call cost. The 87.5% figures describe this narrower, complexity-focused corpus, not a re-measurement of the full V0.2/V0.3 difficulty spread; they should not be read as a claim that the planner's overall unconditional pass rate across every case shape is now 87.5%.
